name: SPECULATION
description: Speculation is a historical gambling game popular in the 18th and 19th centuries, famously depicted in Jane Austen's novels. The game revolves around players buying and selling the right to the 'Highest Trump' currently revealed. It is not trick-taking but a game of chance and negotiation, where the winner is the holder of the highest trump when all cards are revealed.

content.text: Speculation is a historical gambling game popular in the 18th and 19th centuries, famously depicted in Jane Austen's novels. The game revolves around players buying and selling the right to the 'Highest Trump' currently revealed. It is not trick-taking but a game of chance and negotiation, where the winner is the holder of the highest trump when all cards are revealed.

This mild domestic gambling game appeared towards the end of the 18th century and disappeared about a hundred years later. Jane Austen mentions it in Mansfield Park; Dickens in Nicholas Nickleby (1839). Charles Pardon in The Card Player (1868) called it 'without a rival' for Christmas parties. It appears in Cassell's Indoor Amusements (1881) but was omitted from Foster's Complete Hoyle (1897), by which time it was on its way out.
Three to nine players; Hoyle (1874) describes it as a round game for several players, with the dealer and each other contributing to the pool.
Standard 52-card pack, the same as at whist; used with fish or counters on which a value is fixed by the company.
Chips or counters (fish) with agreed value.
Ante into a pot. Deal 3 cards face-down to each player. Top card of deck turned for Trump Suit.

items.text: Five or Jack adds to pot: Anyone turning up a Five or a Jack adds one chip to the pot (Irish-style addition).
Spare hand variant: A spare hand is dealt and revealed at the end; if it contains a higher trump than the apparent winner's, the pot remains and is added to the next deal.
